mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which elevates input costs and suppresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% over two months signals a deflationary monetary easing, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls and CPIAUCSL < 2% in the same month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A positive and accelerating growth in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200k per month for three consecutive months, combined with an unemployment rate below 5%, signals a tight labor market that boosts wage pressure and inflation risk, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE < 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly above zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio rising above its 5-year average for six consecutive months) signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces aggregate demand and corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.
